title: Laced vapes: what is in them, how they reach children, and how to report sellers
excerpt: Vapes sold to children as cannabis oil are being found to contain spice, a far stronger synthetic drug that has put young people in hospital. Here is what is known and how to report sellers in Rochdale.
body:
Vapes sold to children as cannabis oil are being found to contain spice, a synthetic drug far stronger than the cannabis it imitates, and young people across England have ended up in hospital after using them.

The vapes are usually advertised as “THC” liquid, the active ingredient in cannabis. Dealers swap in spice without telling buyers because it is cheaper, and its strength is unpredictable.

Research by Professor Chris Pudney, of the University of Bath, found in 2025 that as many as one in four vapes confiscated in schools contained spice.

He has identified a network of about 10,000 social media accounts linked to selling it, with “THC vape liquid” advertised for as little as £2. A genuine THC vape typically costs £60 to £80.

In June, ITV News reported the case of a boy who began using what he thought was a THC vape at 12. After about two months of daily use he collapsed, suffered a collapsed lung and spent two weeks in an induced coma.

In Hull, two 13-year-old girls were taken to hospital in April after being handed a vape at a park. Tests found spice and MDMA, according to their mother.

Most of the selling happens on social media, including Snapchat, TikTok and Instagram. Professor Pudney described it as overt drug dealing, with the platforms used as shop windows.

TikTok and Snapchat both say illegal vape sales are banned on their platforms and that they remove such content. Ofcom, which regulates the platforms under the Online Safety Act, says selling drugs to children is illegal and that it will act where platforms fall short.

In Rochdale borough, the council's trading standards team obtained closure orders against six shops in six months to December 2025 for illegal tobacco and vapes, including the Green Shop in Heywood, where illegal vapes were found in the shop and in a car linked to the business.

In June, Rochdale's neighbourhood police and trading standards carried out checks on shops in Milnrow and Littleborough for sales of vapes and alcohol to under-18s, and said the checks would continue regularly.

Parents are advised to warn children never to accept or share a vape from someone they do not know. If a child collapses, has a seizure or struggles to breathe after vaping, call 999.

Information about people selling drugs can be given to Greater Manchester Police on 101 or online at gmp.police.uk, or anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

Sources: ITV News; University of Bath; Rochdale Borough Council; Greater Manchester Police. Photograph: Rochdale Daily library.
